thought.text: Both serving modes verified. Cleaning up my test servers to restore the original state:

reasoning_content:
Both the dev server and the static dist build are working. I'll terminate the test server (cleanup), confirm that port 8080 is free again, and complete the evaluation.

Actually, should I keep the dev server running or stop it? The original final state was "the dev server is not currently running." To restore the original state, I should stop the background server I started (both the webpack dev server on port 8080 and the static server on port 8081).

Let me terminate by specifying the exact PID. I'll find the PID.

action.command: pkill -f "python3 -m http.server 8081"; WPIDS=$(ps aux | grep -E 'webpack|npm start|node .*webpack' | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2}'); echo "webpack pids: $WPIDS"; for p in $WPIDS; do kill $p 2>/dev/null; done; sleep 3; ps aux | grep -E 'webpack|http.server' | grep -v grep; echo "---ports after cleanup---"; for f in /proc/net/tcp /proc/net/tcp6; do [ -f "$f" ] && awk 'NR>1 && $4=="0A" {split($2,a,":"); printf "%d\n", ("0x" a[2])+0}' "$f"; done | sort -un; echo "done"

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "pkill -f \"python3 -m http.server 8081\"; WPIDS=$(ps aux | grep -E 'webpack|npm start|node .*webpack' | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2}'); echo \"webpack pids: $WPIDS\"; for p in $WPIDS; do kill $p 2>/dev/null; done; sleep 3; ps aux | grep -E 'webpack|http.server' | grep -v grep; echo \"---ports after cleanup---\"; for f in /proc/net/tcp /proc/net/tcp6; do [ -f \"$f\" ] && awk 'NR>1 && $4==\"0A\" {split($2,a,\":\"); printf \"%d\\n\", (\"0x\" a[2])+0}' \"$f\"; done | sort -un; echo \"done\"", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Stop test servers and verify ports freed"}

summary: Stop test servers and verify ports freed
